english.title: Provide early years childminding when enforcement notice in effect
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) contravened an enforcement notice issued under section 33(4) of the Childcare Act 2006 in that without reasonable excuse you provided early years childminding without being registered as an early years childminder in the early years register or with an early years childminder agency
english.legislation: Contrary to section 33(7) and (8) of the Childcare Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 33(2) of the Childcare Act 2006 allows the Secretary of State to provide exceptions to the requirement to register.
(ii) This offence no longer applies after the 31st October 2024 due to changes made by the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023. For the offence applying after this date, see H101867.
english.standardstatementoffacts:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant contravened an enforcement notice issued under section 33(4) of the Childcare Act 2006 in that without reasonable excuse

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

provided early years childminding without being registered as an early years childminder in the early years register or with an early years childminder agency.

other.penalty:
Summary: a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecution:
Six months from the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the prosecutor to warrant the proceedings comes to his knowledge, but no more than three years after the commission of the offence.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
